proof:
The endpoint triangle has area $1/2$ and the middle triangle has area $3/2$ by their vertex determinants. The facets of $B$ have inequalities $2x+y\le1$, $-x+y\le1$, $-x-2y\le1$. The midpoint body $(K-K)/2$ has vertices $(1/2,0)$, $(0,1/2)$, $(-1/2,1/2)$ and their opposites. All satisfy the inequalities, with equality respectively at $(1/2,0)$ for the first, $(-1/2,1/2)$ for the second, and $(0,-1/2)$ for the third. A representation of base zero has equal endpoint coefficients. Therefore the midpoint inclusion suffices for every anchored inclusion at zero, and the extreme bases are unchanged in the lifted convex hull. Its base projection is $[-1,1]$, so these are the exact integer fibers. The positive fibers at distinct bases make the hull full dimensional. A symmetry center would have base zero and would exchange $K$ and $-K$, forcing its continuous component to be zero by boundedness. But the negative of $(1,-1)$ violates the second facet inequality of $B$.

The maps
$$
R_0(x,y)=(-y,-x),\qquad R_1(x,y)=(-x,x+y),\qquad R_2(x,y)=(x+y,-y)
$$
are involutions of determinant $-1$ by their matrices. Each permutes the displayed vertices of $B$, preserves $x^2+xy+y^2$ by substitution and satisfies $l_i\circ R_i=-l_i$. Thus $B_\varepsilon$ is invariant under each $R_i$. The two corresponding central halfplanes have equal area in $B_\varepsilon$ because $R_i$ exchanges them and their common line is area-null. Also $E=-E$, so the new midpoint is $(K-K)/2+\varepsilon E\subseteq B+\varepsilon E$. Its support gap to $B_\varepsilon$ is at least $\varepsilon h_E(u)\ge\varepsilon\sqrt{2/3}$ for each unit $u$, since $x^2+xy+y^2\le(3/2)(x^2+y^2)$. The exact-fiber argument still applies. This margin also gives an open neighborhood of compatible independent fiber changes, since the midpoint support gap can change by at most twice the maximum Hausdorff change of the fibers.

The three affine cap margins sum to zero, so their halfspaces cover the ambient space. At base $1$ the $i$th trace is $l_i\ge a_i-1/3$, while reflection sends its base $-1$ trace to $l_i\le a_i-1/3$ on $A_\varepsilon$. Their common line has zero area. The two endpoint contributions thus sum to $|A_\varepsilon|$ for every such threshold. The base-zero trace is $l_i\ge0$ independently of $a$ and contributes $|B_\varepsilon|/2$, giving the exact budget $\widehat M_\varepsilon/2$. The common dilation and change of cap equations multiply all masses by $\alpha_\varepsilon^2$. The dilated fibers tend to the original fibers since $\alpha_\varepsilon\to1$.

Finally $\{2x+y\le0\}$ captures total endpoint area $|K|=1/2$ by reflection. On the middle triangle its vertex values are $1,1,-2$, so the retained triangle has edge fractions $2/3,2/3$ at the negative vertex. Its area is $(4/9)(3/2)=2/3$, giving $7/6$ altogether.

statement:
In the mixed space with one integer base coordinate $z$ and two continuous coordinates $(x,y)$, use the fibers $-K,B,K$ at $-1,0,1$, where
$$
K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1/3,-1/3),(2/3,-1/3),(-1/3,2/3)\},\qquad
B=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,-1),(0,1),(-1,0)\}.
$$
Their lifted convex hull has exactly these integer fibers, has total fiber area $M=5/2$, and is nonsymmetric. The endpoint Minkowski midpoint touches each facet of $B$. Put $E=\{(x,y):x^2+xy+y^2\le1\}$ and, for $\varepsilon\ge0$, take the rounded fibers $-A_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon,A_\varepsilon$, where $A_\varepsilon=K+\varepsilon E$ and $B_\varepsilon=B+2\varepsilon E$. For $\varepsilon>0$ their midpoint support slack is at least $\varepsilon\sqrt{2/3}$ in all unit directions. If $l_0(x,y)=-x-y$, $l_1(x,y)=x$, $l_2(x,y)=y$, then for each $a$ near $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$ with $\sum_i a_i=1$, the three caps $H_i(a)=\{l_i(x,y)-(a_i-1/3)z\ge0\}$ cover the ambient space and each has half the rounded total mass $\widehat M_\varepsilon$. Dilation of all fibers by $\alpha_\varepsilon=(M/\widehat M_\varepsilon)^{1/2}$ fixes total mass at $M$ and fixes the transformed budgets at $5/4$, with the base coefficient in each cap multiplied by $\alpha_\varepsilon$. On the original body the through-origin cap $\{2x+y\le0\}$ has mass $7/6$.
title: Three reflections give cap-budget-flat rounding of an active nonsymmetric source
